rules.title: Target declares no launch screen
rules.why: An app with no launch screen is letterboxed at a legacy resolution on modern devices. Review sees an app that does not fill the screen and rejects it as incomplete.
resolutions: Add a UILaunchScreen dictionary to Info.plist, empty if the launch screen is a plain background
Or set UILaunchStoryboardName to a launch storyboard included in the target's resources

rules.title: UIWebView used instead of WKWebView
rules.why: Apple requires the current WebKit framework for apps that browse the web. UIWebView was removed from the SDK and its presence is caught by automated validation as ITMS-90809.

clauses.note: Match the type name, not the substring — WKWebViewConfiguration must not fire this.

resolutions: Replace UIWebView with WKWebView, including in any XIB or storyboard that instantiates it

cases.symptom: Upload rejected with ITMS-90809: Deprecated API Usage — the app still linked UIWebView
cases.root_cause: UIWebView was deprecated in iOS 12 and removed from the SDK; Apple's automated pipeline rejects binaries referencing it, including references reaching the binary only through a dependency

rules.title: Symbol matching a known private API appears in source
rules.why: Apps may only use public APIs. Apple's static scanner matches selector names, so a private selector reached through a string or a runtime call is still found.

clauses.note: Apple's scanner matches SELECTOR NAMES, not intent, so a developer's own method that happens to share a name with a private selector is a genuine false positive. Confirm the symbol resolves to a system class before emitting, and downgrade to PROBABLE where it resolves to app-owned code.
A leading underscore in a runtime-resolved selector string is the shape Apple's scanner looks for.

resolutions: Replace the call with a public API, or remove it
Where the symbol is app-owned and merely shares a name with a private selector, rename it so the scanner does not match

rules.title: Executable code is downloaded or evaluated at runtime
rules.why: Apps must be self-contained and may not download or execute code that changes their features. This is one of the few guidelines Apple treats as grounds for removal rather than rejection.

clauses.note: evaluateJavaScript against bundled, app-authored script is normal and must not fire; the concern is script fetched from a server.

resolutions: Ship the logic in the binary and gate it with a remote configuration flag rather than downloading the logic itself
Where the code is bundled and merely loaded dynamically, confirm nothing on the path can be replaced from the network

rules.title: Version string or app name marks the build as a beta or demo
rules.why: Demos, betas and trial versions belong on TestFlight, not the App Store. A version string of 0.x or a name containing beta is read as an unfinished submission.
resolutions: Set CFBundleShortVersionString to a 1.0 or later release version
Remove beta, demo or staging wording from the display name

rules.title: Placeholder text or unimplemented screens remain in shipping code
rules.why: App completeness is the single largest cause of rejection by volume. Lorem ipsum, a Coming Soon screen or a TODO in a user-visible string is read as an unfinished app.

clauses.note: Only user-visible string literals. A TODO in a comment is not shipped content and must not fire.

resolutions: Replace the placeholder with final content
Remove the screen from navigation if the feature is not in this release

rules.title: A literal IPv4 address is used for a network endpoint
rules.why: Apps must be fully functional on IPv6-only networks, and Apple reviews on one. A hardcoded IPv4 literal cannot resolve there, so the app fails review while working perfectly for the developer.

clauses.note: Matches an IPv4 anywhere inside a string literal, not just at its start — the common case is an address inside a URL, where http:// sits between the quote and the digits. Loopback and 0.0.0.0 are excluded. A version string such as 1.2.3.4 in a non-URL context is a false positive worth confirming.

resolutions: Replace the literal address with a hostname that has both A and AAAA records
Where the address is test-only, move it behind a debug configuration that does not ship

rules.title: A background mode is declared that no code appears to use
rules.why: Background modes may only be used for their intended purpose. Apple rejects apps declaring a mode — most often location or audio — with no corresponding functionality, because it reads as an attempt to stay alive.
resolutions: Remove the background mode the app does not use
Or implement the functionality the declared mode exists for, and be ready to describe it in review notes

rules.title: A remote flag gates functionality that review cannot see
rules.why: Apps may not include hidden, dormant or undocumented features. A feature behind a server-controlled flag is functionality review did not evaluate, and enabling it after approval is grounds for removal.

clauses.note: A flag whose NAME references App Review is the strong signal. A generic feature flag is normal engineering and must not fire on its own.

resolutions: Remove logic that changes behaviour when the reviewer is detected
Where the flag is a legitimate rollout control, document it in review notes and ensure the reviewed build shows the shipped behaviour

rules.title: Target is iPhone-only
rules.why: Apple asks that iPhone apps run on iPad wherever possible. This is a recommendation rather than a rejection, so it is reported as a quality signal, not a blocker.
resolutions: Set TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY to 1,2 and verify the layout on iPad before submitting
Leave iPhone-only if the app depends on hardware iPad lacks, and expect a reviewer to check that it does

rules.title: An API newer than the deployment target is called without an availability check
rules.why: Calling a symbol the deployment target predates crashes on the older OS. Review tests on more than one OS version, and a crash there is rejected under app completeness as well as this guideline.

clauses.note: Only meaningful where the source uses APIs above the deployment target; the subagent must confirm at least one such symbol before emitting.

resolutions: Wrap the call in if #available(iOS n, *) and provide a path for older versions
Or raise IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET to the version the API requires

rules.title: App icon asset is missing or has an alpha channel
rules.why: A missing or transparent app icon fails automated validation on upload. Transparency in particular is accepted by Xcode and rejected by App Store Connect.
resolutions: Add an AppIcon set with a 1024x1024 App Store icon and no alpha channel
Set ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME on the target to the icon set's name

rules.title: Layout uses hardcoded device dimensions rather than size classes
rules.why: A layout built on literal screen dimensions breaks in Split View and on device sizes it was not written for. This is the layout defect reviewers most often reproduce on iPad.

clauses.note: UIScreen.main.bounds read once for a full-screen background is normal; arithmetic against it to position content is the pattern that breaks.

resolutions: Lay out against the safe area and size classes rather than absolute screen dimensions
Verify the layout in Split View and Slide Over on iPad before submitting

rules.title: App and extension declare different App Group identifiers
rules.why: A widget or extension reading a shared container under a different group identifier silently gets nothing. Review sees a widget that never populates, which is rejected as incomplete functionality.

clauses.note: Compare the value across every shipping target; the finding exists only when two targets disagree.

resolutions: Use the same App Group identifier in every target that shares the container
Where the divergence is intentional, confirm no target reads data another target writes

rules.title: A declared URL scheme collides with a scheme Apple reserves
rules.why: Registering a scheme the system owns, or querying prefs:root= to open Settings, is treated as using a non-public interface.
resolutions: Rename the scheme to one namespaced to the app, such as the reverse-DNS bundle identifier
Replace prefs:root= with UIApplication.openSettingsURLString, which is the public route to the app's own settings

rules.title: Face-based account authentication built on ARKit or a camera API
rules.why: Apps using facial recognition for account authentication must use LocalAuthentication, not ARKit or raw camera capture. Rolling your own face auth is a rejection regardless of how well it works.

clauses.note: Face tracking for an avatar, a filter or a measurement is legitimate. The rule is about face data used to AUTHENTICATE, which the subagent must confirm.

resolutions: Use LAContext with .deviceOwnerAuthenticationWithBiometrics for authentication
Where the face tracking drives a feature rather than a login, no change is needed — confirm the two paths do not join

rules.title: Screenshots show this build in use, at every required size
rules.why_manual: Screenshots are uploaded to App Store Connect. The repository does not contain them and cannot know which ones are attached to this version.
rules.why: Screenshots must show the app in use rather than a title card or a device frame with marketing copy, and must be current for the build under review.
resolutions: Retake screenshots from this build on the current required device sizes, showing the app actually running

rules.title: App name, subtitle and keywords describe what the app does
rules.why_manual: Name, subtitle and keywords live in App Store Connect metadata, not in the bundle.
rules.why: Apple rejects names and keywords that claim functionality the app lacks, reference competitors, or stuff irrelevant terms.
resolutions: Check the name, subtitle and keyword list against what this build actually does, and remove competitor and unrelated terms

rules.title: What's New text describes this submission
rules.why_manual: Release notes are entered per version in App Store Connect.
rules.why: What's New must describe the changes in this version. Carrying the previous version's text over is a metadata inaccuracy.
resolutions: Write release notes describing what changed in this build

rules.title: Category and age rating match the app's actual content
rules.why_manual: Category selection and the age-rating questionnaire are answered in App Store Connect.
rules.why: Choosing a category the app does not fit, or under-declaring the age rating, are both metadata rejections and both are checked by a human reviewer.
resolutions: Confirm the primary category matches the app's main function, and that the age-rating answers reflect the content this build ships

rules.title: Demo account credentials are supplied for a login-gated app
rules.why_manual: Demo credentials live in the App Store Connect review-notes field and their validity depends on a live backend. Neither is in the repository.
rules.why: An app behind a login must give review a working account. A missing or expired demo account is one of the fastest rejections there is, and it is entirely avoidable.
resolutions: Provide a working demo account in App Store Connect review notes, and verify it can sign in on the day of submission

rules.title: Recording or streaming user activity without explicit consent and a visible indicator
rules.why: 2.5.14 requires explicit consent and a clear visual or audible indicator whenever an app records, logs or otherwise makes a record of user activity — including a screen, camera or microphone feed sent off the device. A capture pipeline with no consent prompt and no on-screen indicator is the shape this clause was written for.

clauses.note: A capture API used entirely on-device and shown back to the user in the same view — a camera preview, an AR passthrough — is not a recording of user activity. What 2.5.14 is about is a record that persists or leaves the device. AVCaptureVideoDataOutput driving an ARKit or Vision pipeline frame by frame, with no writer and no peer connection, is the common false positive.

resolutions: Ask for explicit consent before the capture starts, and record that the user gave it
Show a visible or audible indicator for as long as the capture runs, in the app's own UI rather than relying on the system status indicator alone
If the capture never persists and never leaves the device, no consent flow is required — confirm that is the case rather than assuming it
